# #2542 Family 143: Native Pipeline Mutation And Timer Retirement

## Boundary And Closure

Binding source ruling: issue comment 6088792318. Stack base b670e2b5f; no
freshness rebase, new issue, PR, framework, compatibility path or vendoring.
The last six roots are converted and have positive execution evidence.
The complete recordingRuntimeMutationRunner constructor/consumer chain is
deleted, including handwritten schemas, raw transaction contexts, lifecycle,
query, readiness, timer and mutation-journal interpreters. The conservative
plain-call tail is zero; the stronger owned-source identifier/method guard
also rejects the retired capabilities throughout the pipeline source tree.

Chosen class: ordinary pipeline fixture consumers treating fake transaction,
construction and persistence interpreters as selected runtime authority.
Immediate parent: shared fixture authority escapes; broader parent: #2542/#2151
selected-store capability confinement. The observed helper was an entry point,
not the boundary. The family aims to eliminate its chosen class entirely; parent
closure is not claimed. Achieved level is capability retirement with native
consumer execution and owner guards, pending independent checkpoint review.
The whole historical codemod suite is NOT green; see the explicit blocker below.
This checkpoint is not landing-ready or final integrated qualification.

Governing references:
`engine.runtime_core_persistence_store_contracts.selected_contracts`,
selected_runtime_store_projection/raw_sql_policy and
selected_runtime_mutation_unit_of_work; fixed process source and
dynamic_instance_lifecycle.creation.process. Authoritative platform-spec.yaml
adds native mutation/timer, prospective-source and human-requester fixture rules.

The delegating observer attaches before construction/activation when consumers capture it, and covers the complete execution window. |
| Existing timer lifecycle, scheduler and runtime work occurrence | Initial/event, cause-scoped, declaration/reentry, mode, cancellation, recurring/retry, deadline/join and recovery/reopen consumers use these same original owners. Predecessor stop/join precedes close/reopen. Reconciliation receives genuinely issued attachment authority. |

Foreign-requester read collaboration mutates no authority; exact continuation and write counters remain unchanged. Successful routing commits once and dispatches only after the transaction is inactive. |
| Private mutationlog and pipelinepersistence fault owners | Fixed missing-domain-path, exact timer and projection-shape faults run only under the original selected writer coordinator. They retain exact run/entity/activation validation, cancellation, rollback and restoration. Registry adds 46 specific private backend/adapter findings, not ordinary-consumer permissions. |
| Finite codemod and owned-source guards | Historical Before/After pins remain unchanged. Six exact successor/retirement records plus the inherited timer failure-message update have explicit current cuts. Removed functions must remain absent; surviving/ambiguous definitions, changed successor bodies and missing required files fail closed. |

Old ordinary SQL paths are invalid, not aliases or delegates. Twelve fixture
files are deleted. Value-only mutate/mutateE now commit through the original
closed owner. Pure malformed publication plans and unissued value-model identity
remain adversarial component controls only, never storage, claim or grant
authority. No DB getter or raw transaction context remains in this family.
The original PostgreSQL outer-transaction proof stays PostgreSQL scoped.
The original SQLite-only component scopes are not advertised as public parity.
Reopen and current-source cases retain both-backend execution.

## Source And Temporal Corrections

Prospective source B is NOT live source replacement: A's original interceptor
returns the exact stale-declaration refusal after occurrence/publication commit.
The current admitted-source positive uses live administrative context but must
publish mock from the durable activation. No interceptor replacement or production
admission change. Cause-scoped retirement now wires the same scheduler into both
existing references; no timer policy change. Human fixtures persist an actual reply
context and eligible requester, carry the complete canonical root route, and use
real deferral/expiry rather than fabricating final card states. Eight newly orphaned
helpers are removed, including two dead production formatting functions; no live
production behavior or timing contract changes.

- guard-closure.jsonl: PASS, nine roots, including actual candidate type overlay,
  complete capability absence, immutable historical recipe proofs, exact current
  successor pins, constructor retirement and native source/publication ownership.
- whole-store-guards.jsonl: PASS, store and runtimepersistence structural guards,
  hostile authority controls, executable-delivery confinement and existing inventories.
- codemod-inert.json: actual dry run is inert: Write=false, Changes=[].
- final-global-census.jsonl: PASS, final census and registry, 175.885s; total
  residual 10,942 findings / 7,946 raw sites / 67 excluded uncertainties. Relative
  to b670e2b5f: 774 findings and 574 raw sites removed, zero added identities.
- final-preflight-controls.jsonl: PASS, malformed retirement metadata,
  successor hostility, syntax/read failure and all-or-nothing preflight controls.
- unused-corrected.log: native default/race/issue2413 sweep; no cross-platform claim.
- complexity/: exact committed-head comparison required before push.

The first whole-codemod run was RED: fifteen root failures, then its five-minute
outer command limit interrupted a later type-overlay control. No timeout was
raised, no retry-until-green, skip, guard waiver or narrowed production scan.
The family-owned absence/source-pinning failures are repaired and independently
green in guard-closure.jsonl.

Ten remaining historical workload-preservation roots reproduce against the
frozen approved b670e2b5f ledger using approved-ledger-contrast.jsonl. That is a
source-pinned ledger contrast, NOT clean-base runtime qualification. Their
Before/After models conflate the old mechanical migration with subsequently
approved native construction corrections: canonical parent identity, construction
publication reads, required capability wiring and extracted shared setup. No
unrelated model rewrite or blanket pin refresh was retained. These ten failures
remain a concrete proof-bookkeeping integration blocker under existing #2542;
they are not waived or counted as passing. The original failed receipts and
contrast are retained. A final landing still needs their repair and integrated
qualification.

## Parent, Watchlist And Architecture

Existing #2542/#2151 fixture-authority and full-lifecycle watchlist mappings remain;
no new node or issue. M09 is still unclassified in #2353, not disposed of here.
The parent remains open: approximately 7,946 confirmed raw-operation debt sites
plus its strict completion/SQLite fork-deadline/integrated finish line remain.
This is occurrence debt, not a bug count or closure percentage; grouping/rate
must be reassessed after the next high-fan-out family. No unnamed follow-up split.

Architecture disposition: promote existing domain owners now. Remaining smell is
historical proof snapshots mixing mechanical transforms with later semantic setup
repairs. The long-run direction is separate immutable transformation receipts from
explicit current semantic successors, using the existing finite codemod, not a
second inventory or restoration framework. Tracking stays #2542 and its checklist.
Expected narrow proof-model repair is roughly half a day, medium confidence, high
ROI because it restores repeatable guard qualification without weakening execution.
No parent closure or merge approval is implied by this checkpoint.

Timing: last human roots 40.303s including race runtime, changed compiled-history
root 13.245s, complete family guard closure 68.515s, whole store guards 62.008s,
corrected census/registry 32.067s, final receipt 175.885s under concurrent native
analysis. Setup/owner investigation and the diagnosed
historical proof models remain the dominant cost, not the last six executions.
